name: Shadwell expansive-working pump
summary: A Watt pumping engine at the Shadwell waterworks in London that ran with steam cut off part-way through each stroke, an early working use of expansive steam.
description: Watt pumping engine at Shadwell waterworks applying steam cutoff and subsequent expansion during the piston stroke.
tier_reason: A particular pumping application fits fine detail. Shadwell operating details remain a historian flag rather than being silently settled from Smiles. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: The waterworks needed steady pumping to supply London customers, and working steam expansively promised lower fuel use.
